Statement: I’m Steve Kromer, and I’m running for City Council in District 1. I’ve had many addresses in Berkeley over the last 37 years, but good luck, and my dog Wilson, led me to the neighborhood I now call home. You can find us at James Kenney Park almost every morning. That’s my first reason for running: I love this park. I run the Friends of James Kenney Park email list and help organize our clean-up days, working alongside the neighbors and volunteers who look after the place we share. Parks are where a neighborhood becomes a community. Second, transparency. I’ve spent my career measuring whether public dollars deliver what they promise — as a Professional Engineer and a nonprofit treasurer. Our parks’ budgets, and the city’s, should be open and honest. You deserve to see where your money goes. Third, efficient city government. Berkeley doesn’t lack good ideas — it lacks follow- through. I know how to turn plans into results that hold up after the meeting ends. Running for office is how I give back. Democracy starts at home, in our neighborhoods and parks. My first promise as your representative is simple: I will listen. Really listen. Listen, listen, listen.

Berkeley faces two questions: how do we deliver effective, fiscally-responsible city services, and how do we uphold our progressive values and protect our most vulnerable neighbors? Too many politicians tell us we must choose. I don’t believe that. My name is Daria Wrubel, and I’m running to prove Berkeley can be both well run and true to its values. I’m a lifelong Berkeley resident, a former Berkeley public school garden teacher, a licensed marriage and family therapist, and a former union organizer. I’ve spent years helping our young people through a mental health system that too often fails them. As an organizer, I learned that real change comes from bringing people together, not driving them apart. I’m running to build housing and protect tenants, because those goals belong together. I’m running to invest in public safety that keeps us safe without mass- surveillance, and without risking further harm to immigrants, trans neighbors, and everyone the current federal administration has targeted. District 1 residents deserve experienced representation that delivers for them and their neighbors. Learn more about my campaign and how you can join us at https://www.dariaforberkeley.com/. I’d be honored to earn your vote.

Proudly endorsed by the Berkeley Fire Fighters Association, Local 1227. Berkeley City Council needs leaders with a proven record of governing effectively, managing public dollars responsibly, and delivering results for the people they serve. With an estimated $30M deficit, our neighborhood cannot afford another politician more focused on satisfying lobbyists than serving our community. We need a leader who listens, understands government, and turns priorities into results. That is why I am running. I learned during my 10 years as an education advocate that no one will fight for your kids like you will. So, I stepped up. As an elected official, I made fiscal oversight and accountability a priority while increasing pay, saving jobs, prioritizing student outcomes, advancing climate sustainability, and building educator housing. I’m ready to bring that same governing experience to District One. As a Financial Controller managing global budgets, I know fiscal management is essential. Our tax dollars must protect our first responders, build truly affordable housing, keep our streets paved, address homelessness with lasting solutions, and help small businesses thrive. My family has called District One home for generations. I know its strengths, experience its challenges, and will fight for those who live here today. Proudly endorsed by State Senator Jesse Arreguin. Vote Laura Babitt! www.laura4d1.com Listen. Connect. Deliver.

I’m running for City Council to build an affordable, safe, green, and thriving Berkeley for everyone. I’ve spent the past 15 years working on environmental efforts around the world, and now I’m excited to focus my efforts on my local community. As a new father, I’m committed to keeping our community safe and welcoming, making it easier to get around for people of all abilities, and working to ensure we create more housing at all income levels so our kids can afford to live here when they grow up. As Councilmember, I’ll green our community by planting more trees, advocating for our parks, and fighting climate change with clean energy and sustainable transportation. I’ll support our first responders and local businesses, fix our streets and sidewalks, and work to tackle our housing and homelessness crises with citywide solutions and regional partners. I bring a pragmatic, progressive perspective to ensuring Berkeley delivers exceptional city services and spends tax dollars wisely. I will prioritize constituent services. I’m proud to be endorsed by the Berkeley Firefighters Association, the Sierra Club, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, along with additional elected and community leaders. I hope to earn your vote as well. Join us: www.RossForBerkeley.com

Repair Our Streets. Save Our Waterfront. Keep Flock Out. As your city council representative, I will forward an agenda of accountability, affordability, and community. Working at the California Public Utilities Commission, I am proud to hold a record of achievement on clean energy initiatives, utility regulation, and protecting everyday Californians from fraud. As someone who has revised billion-dollar budgets, I am not afraid to take on our ballooning deficit and balance our City’s budget. I will work with the city to maintain infrastructure, expand climate resilience, and provide dignified housing and services for the unhoused. Berkeley needs a community-centered vision. Working with community land trusts and non-profits, I will focus on building on our successes in affordable housing growth, while expanding community and open spaces. I will work to improve tenant protections and fight housing speculation that results in empty building shells and pushes out our local businesses. I will develop green spaces in West Berkeley and protect our waterfront. Berkeley can be a more affordable city — a sustainable city that supports its residents and improves the quality of life for all. As our city grows and changes, we must live by the guiding principle: We take care of us.

I am Majdi Gaith, an independent progressive, former Peace and Justice Commissioner, Trust and Safety policy professional, small business co- founder, parent, and UC Berkeley graduate running for Berkeley City Council, District 4. For more than a decade, I have developed policies that protect millions of people from harassment, fraud, abuse, and emerging threats. This work taught me how to evaluate evidence, solve complex problems, build consensus, and make balanced decisions that strengthen public trust. I am building a multicultural, multifaith, and multigenerational coalition because Berkeley is strongest when people from every background and generation work together. As the co-founder of a local coffee roasting business and bakery, I understand the challenges facing small businesses, workers, and our neighborhood commercial corridors. As a parent raising a family in Berkeley, I know every resident deserves safe streets, reliable city services, attainable housing, and the opportunity to thrive. I will bring thoughtful leadership, fiscal responsibility, transparency, and integrity to City Hall. I will work to revitalize downtown and our neighborhood commercial corridors, strengthen tenant protections, support workers and local businesses, expand housing opportunities, improve public safety, advance climate action, and ensure Berkeley’s government is accountable, responsive, and committed to protecting the rights, dignity, and opportunity of every resident.

When you elected me two years ago, I promised to be accessible, attentive, and focused on solving our city’s most pressing needs. Together we secured new housing at every income level, including affordable homes downtown; advanced street safety and accessibility improvements across our district; brought Downtown commercial vacancies down to pre-pandemic levels while investing in our small businesses and the arts; and reopened Civic Center Park as a public commons that everyone can enjoy. Still, we face challenges, including significant federal budget cuts and rising costs. I’m placing my decades of experience to work for you. We must continue to advance homeownership opportunities and rentals that hardworking residents can afford, help the unhoused find the supportive housing and wraparound services they deserve, and implement safer, climate-resilient infrastructure. I’m proud to be endorsed by the Sierra Club, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon, California Attorney General Rob Bonta, Mayor Adena Ishii, supermajorities of the City Council and Rent Board, every Berkeley School Boardmember, Supervisor Nikki Fortunato Bas, State Senators Jesse Arreguín and Aisha Wahab, Alameda County Sheriff Yesenia Sanchez our BART, AC Transit, East Bay Regional Parks, and East Bay Municipal Utility District directors, and 100+ neighbors and community leaders. We’re just getting started. I’d be honored to earn your vote for a full term so we can continue to make Berkeley a place we can all call home. www.IgorTregub.com

District 7 is my home. I live on Telegraph and have lived in Southside since 2016. I am a UC Berkeley graduate and clinical health worker who previously served as Vice Chair of Berkeley’s Homeless Commission. There, I moved and amended the People’s First Sanctuary Encampment recommendation, which centered clean water, sanitation, privacy, and resident decision-making. I have organized around People’s Park since 2017 and served meals through East Bay Food Not Bombs. I’m running because Southside needs a councilmember who can turn community needs into practical city action. I will protect rent-controlled housing and expand permanent affordability. I will prioritize sidewalk, lighting, sanitation, and disability-access improvements. I will work to make major development fund the infrastructure its growth demands and press UC Berkeley for housing and neighborhood responsibility. I will seek voter approval before major public land is converted and publish quarterly progress reports on housing stability, street repairs, public space, and local business conditions. Students, renters, workers, local business owners, and longtime neighbors deserve a councilmember they can reach and results they can see. I ask for your first-choice vote. https://www.aidanhill.vote

I was born, raised, and educated in Berkeley, graduating from UC Berkeley with degrees in Economics and Public Policy in December 2025. As an organizer and student advocate, I’m deeply committed to making Berkeley more affordable and accessible to students and marginalized community members. In 2024, I was elected as the Transfer Student Representative in the Associated Students of the University of California. I worked towards the creation of re-entry student housing and wrote grants for lighting across University Village. At Cal, I was a member of the “Black Triad” (African American Student Development, Black Student Union, and Black Recruitment and Retention Center), Cal Young Democratic Socialists of America, and the Berkeley Student Food Collective. During my last semester at Cal I served as a Campus Organizer with the Alameda Labor Council, leading the UC Berkeley “Get Out the Vote” campaign for Prop 50. I have worked with East Bay Alliance for a Sustainable Economy to organize Black workers and build labor power in my community. Currently, I serve on Berkeley’s Housing Advisory Commission for District 7. There, I have voted to hold landlords accountable, fund improved housing infrastructure, support affordable housing development, and renovate existing affordable housing. I strongly believe that housing is a human right, that living should be affordable, and that everyone should feel safe in our city. I am honored to be endorsed by the East Bay Democratic Socialists of America, UAW Region 6, the Berkeley Tenants Union, Telegraph for People, and Alameda County Supervisor Nikki Fortunato Bas – learn more at syrakforsouthside.com.

It has been a privilege and a pleasure to serve as the District 8 Councilmember for these past four years, and I remain committed to putting essential public services and infrastructure first. In my first term, we’ve enhanced District 8 parks and replaced the Willard Clubhouse with a new, award- winning facility; supported our first responders with superb police and fire chiefs, new technology, and better wildfire preparedness; began investing in smoother, safer streets; updated our zoning laws to enable middle-density homes; and supported community events like the Elmwood Music Festival, Russell Street Halloween, Berkeley Sun Day, and more. There’s still much to be done, so I’m asking for your vote to continue working with you to improve public safety, support our small businesses, fix our streets and sidewalks, and make our city more inclusive and affordable. My pragmatic and collaborative approach is why my colleagues want to work with me for another 4 years. I’m proud to have the endorsements of State Senator Jesse Arreguín, Assemblymember Buffy Wicks, Mayor of Berkeley Adena Ishii and a supermajority of the Berkeley City Council, Berkeley Firefighters Association Local 1227, the Sierra Club, Berkeley School Board Director Jennifer Shanoski, AC Transit Director Jean Walsh, BART Board Director Barnali Ghosh, Peralta Community College Trustee Dyana Delfin-Polk, and more. Join us: www.HumbertForCouncil.com

Having grown up, raising kids, and caring for elderly family members here in Berkeley, I’ve watched our city change over decades. While shifts occur gradually, the cumulative stress on our community is clear. As an engineer, I analyze data to make sound policy decisions rather than serving special interests or selling out our city to large corporations. I am committed to clean, safe streets, supporting public education, and preserving our parks and open spaces for families across all generations. Living in a Zone Zero neighborhood, fire and earthquake safety are urgent priorities; I will foster close collaboration between the city, fire department, and residents so we can survive a major disaster together. Additionally, development must be balanced—protecting small businesses while accounting for traffic and infrastructure. In the university area, housing policy must protect our neighborhoods and student residents from exploitation while ensuring quality of life. Finally, we must proactively engage the University of California, Berkeley to ensure this large entity respects the integrity, value, and character of our city. Join our cause at wallmandistrict8.com.

District 8 deserves an accountable and accessible council representative who listens to residents and small businesses; supports appropriate scale inclusionary housing; fights for public safety initiatives that won’t threaten our privacy; and understands that the vibrant Elmwood commercial district faces many challenges. Throughout the many years I have lived and worked in Berkeley I have devoted my time and energy to community service and civic engagement. I have served as a volunteer and board member for many community organizations, including Berkeley Public Library Foundation, Jewish Family and Community Services and Bay Area Legal Aid. My priorities are to find better ways to build affordable housing in our high resource neighborhoods so that Berkeley can preserve the diversity which makes our community such a wonderful place to live. I have a strong interest in reforming our mental health system and housing the homeless. I want Berkeley to be a city that everyone looks to as a model for the best that a society can provide. For more information on my campaign, please go to my website, www.fredfellerforcouncil.com. I look forward to working with you.

I’m running for City Council District 8 bringing accountable leadership that listens to and respects the needs of Elmwood. I’ll fight hard to preserve it with growth that’s responsible and honors its legacy, which I understand because I’m part of it. I attended Willard Junior High and worked my first job at Colby Pharmacy, a small family business representing its core. I have over 15 years of experience navigating the difficulties of complex issues, including as an elected leader, a Unite Here 2850 union leader, Housing Commission vice-chair and organizer in the Friends of Adeline. Powerful lobbies are influencing leadership to up-zone and infill neighborhoods under the pretense of addressing our so-called housing crisis, including legislation benefitting investors with density bonuses. This doesn’t capture the affordable housing we need and is locally threatening the viability of our small businesses and neighborhood infrastructure, using oversimplified narratives that more is better. It’s not if it’s irresponsible and destructive. What’s required is mindful and responsible leadership who listens and ensures housing, safety, infrastructure, access and accessibility. We can’t afford politics as usual. People have the power. Let’s use ours to vote for accountable leadership and needed change. Vote Mari Nov 3. Electmarimendonca.com
